title: JDK G1 bug crashes with references [in]to jdk.internal.vm.FillerArray, when upgrading to 8.13.0 or 8.13.1
body: After upgrading Elasticsearch from 8.12.2 to 8.13.0, we see intermittent node failures involving jdk.internal.vm.FillerArray. The fatal exceptions appear in different tasks, including write and refresh threads, and claim that FillerArray cannot be used as interfaces such as Lock or Collection. It happens across the nodes and the service stops afterward.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading from Elasticsearch 8.12.2 to 8.13.0, nodes intermittently exit with fatal errors saying jdk.internal.vm.FillerArray does not implement interfaces such as Lock or Collection.
I have seen the exception in both write and refresh threads, and the service stops afterward.
N0.label: N0 intermittent FillerArray crashes reported

symptoms_visible: Sometimes the failure brings down the cluster and sometimes it appears to recover.
The same FillerArray object appears in incompatible casts to unrelated types such as ByteBuffer, Map, Lock, Collection, and LiveVersionMap VersionLookup.
N1.label: N1 runtime configuration and wider failure pattern collected

symptoms_visible: Other affected clusters on Elasticsearch 8.13.0 and 8.13.1 show the same intermittent fatal FillerArray errors at several unrelated call sites.
N2.label: N2 issue reproduced across 8.13 deployments

symptoms_visible: After moving an affected deployment to the Temurin 21.0.3 beta runtime, I have not seen another crash so far, although the cluster has only been under minimal load.
N3.label: N3 JDK 21 trial running without initial crashes

symptoms_visible: After moving off the bundled JDK 22 runtime and running under normal load on JDK 21, the intermittent FillerArray crashes no longer occur.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved on unaffected JDK

question_patterns: Are you using Elasticsearch's bundled JVM, and what JVM and garbage-collector options are configured?
Can you share the relevant contents of jvm.options, including the heap size and collector?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am using the bundled JVM. The heap is fixed at 28 GB with -Xms28g and -Xmx28g, and -XX:+UseG1GC is set. I also have heap-dump, fatal-exit, error-file, and detailed GC logging options enabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am using my own JDK 21 installation with ZGC rather than the bundled JVM and G1.
I am using the bundled JVM with G1, but the heap is 24 GB instead of 28 GB.

edges.comment: Opening report plus reporter messages c1-c3. The original reporter supplied the bundled-JVM configuration, then voluntarily added the varying cluster impact, unrelated cast targets, and OpenJDK issue link.

question_patterns: Is this limited to the original cluster, or can the same FillerArray failure be seen on other upgraded clusters?
Do other affected deployments show the same exception pattern?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We have the same crashes and restarts on another cluster that was upgraded from Elasticsearch 8.9.0 to 8.13.0. It also fails in refresh threads with FillerArray reported where a Map was expected.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No other deployment reproduces it, and rolling the original cluster back to its previous application configuration does not change the crashes.

question_patterns: Does the same failure occur on the next 8.13 patch build?
Have you seen equivalent stack traces on both 8.13.0 and 8.13.1?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. On Elasticsearch 8.13.1 I also see FillerArray reported where a Map was expected, including from LiveVersionMap.pruneTombstones.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I have only reproduced it on 8.13.0 and have not tested 8.13.1.

edges.comment: Messages c4 and c9-c10 from two additional affected operators are folded into the simulated user side. They describe separate 8.13 deployments but the same diagnostic chain: intermittent FillerArray type failures after the upgrade.

question_patterns: If you try an alternative Java runtime, can you paste its exact java -version output and report what happens?
Please provide the vendor and complete version output for the runtime used in the comparison test.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I built a custom image using an Adoptium nightly. Its output is openjdk version "21.0.3-beta" 2024-04-16, Temurin-21.0.3+7-202403202002. There have been no crashes yet, but the cluster has only had minimal load so far and I still need to observe it during the busy period.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same FillerArray crash occurred again under the alternative Java runtime with an equivalent stack trace.
The alternative runtime is another JDK 21 vendor build, and it has also remained stable under the initial light load.

solution.intent: For a self-hosted affected cluster, temporarily replace the bundled runtime with an unaffected JDK 21 build and monitor the cluster under its normal workload.
solution.concrete_example: Build or configure the self-hosted Elasticsearch deployment to use a JDK 21 runtime instead of its bundled runtime, capture java -version, and observe it through the workload period that normally triggers the crash.

edges.comment: Messages c5-c8: participant3 suggested a local JDK 21 workaround for self-hosted clusters; participant2 installed an Adoptium JDK 21 build and supplied raw java -version output. Since the custom runtime was kept in the deployment, this is a persistent system change rather than a measurement-only edge.

solution.intent: Move affected Elasticsearch installations off the bundled JDK 22 runtime implicated in the G1 FillerArray corruption and use the supported build containing the bundled-JDK downgrade, while confirming stability under the workload that previously triggered crashes.
solution.concrete_example: The confirmed mitigation was to return the bundled runtime to JDK 21.0.2; an affected operator independently confirmed that moving to JDK 21.0.3 stopped the crashes. Elasticsearch 8.13.2 shipped the bundled-runtime downgrade.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied FillerArray stack traces, the bundled-G1 configuration, the OpenJDK issue link, and the JDK 21 comparison result. Engineers connected the Elasticsearch upgrade to its bundled JDK 22 change and concluded that a JDK G1 bug was corrupting references; the apparently unrelated Java cast and interface errors are consequences of that JVM fault.

edges.comment: Messages c13-c19 complete the original 8.13 diagnostic chain. The original reporter tied onset to the JDK 22 upgrade, participant2 confirmed stability after moving to JDK 21 under load, and Elasticsearch adopted a bundled JDK 21 downgrade. The later 7.17.22 discussion in c20-c27 concerns a separate deployment whose replaced jvm.options omitted the workaround flags and is intentionally not spliced into this chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as the bundled JDK 22 G1 FillerArray bug, which can leave corrupted references that surface as unrelated ClassCastException and IncompatibleClassChangeError failures throughout Elasticsearch and Lucene.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the upgrade timing, bundled G1 runtime configuration, repeated FillerArray failures at unrelated call sites, reproduction across 8.13 deployments, and disappearance when an affected deployment moves to JDK 21.
Must recommend moving affected installations to an Elasticsearch build with an unaffected bundled JDK, or using an unaffected JDK 21 runtime as the self-hosted workaround.
Must not treat individual Elasticsearch, Lucene, or Netty cast sites as separate application bugs requiring component-specific fixes.
Must ask the user to verify stability under the normal workload that previously triggered the intermittent failures before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Elasticsearch operator who can inspect JVM options, collect long stack traces, build a custom container with another JDK, run java -version, and monitor behavior under production load.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical and evidence-driven; supplies exact logs and runtime output, distinguishes preliminary observations from confirmation, and follows up when workload conditions make a test inconclusive.
